analysis_pieces.title: Fitch Assigns Rodenstock 'B-' IDR; Outlook Stable (Fitch Ratings, 06-Jul-2026; committee 01-Jul-2026)
analysis_pieces.key_findings: Primary source for the current credit picture; read in full from /resources/Rodenstock/. (1) Capital structure as rated: existing EUR840m TLB due Jun-2028 (margin 5%), EUR125m RCF due Dec-2027, plus EUR11m of local facilities that Fitch treats as super senior. (2) Refinancing not done: the rating and Stable Outlook are 'predicated on timely refinancing of maturities in December 2027 and June 2028 on market terms'. Failure to refinance, or to present a credible refinancing plan, 'within the next six months' could lead to negative rating action. Fitch's rating case assumes refinancing in 2027 at a 6% margin (vs 5% now). (3) Leverage: EBITDA leverage 8.5x at end-2025, forecast 8.0x in 2026 and 7.7x in 2027, both still above Fitch's 7.5x downgrade sensitivity. Fitch sees 'limited near-term rating headroom' and calls the sponsor's financial policy aggressive. Financial structure sub-score 'ccc-'. (4) Performance: FY2025 sales EUR493m (FY2024: EUR512.4m, company figure). Fitch-adjusted EBITDA margin 22% and gross margin 61%. Fitch expects a low-single-digit sales decline in 2026 from the GrandVision contract phase-out, then 3.0-3.2% annual growth from 2027. Margin forecast 24.4% in 2026 on cost savings already executed. (5) Cash flow: historically negative FCF, 'particularly weak' in 2025 on lower EBITDA, higher capex, sizeable interest and material restructuring costs. Fitch expects slightly negative FCF near term, then neutral to slightly positive to 2029. Restructuring costs of EUR10m in 2026 and c.EUR5m a year in 2027-28. Pension contributions EUR11-12m a year. No dividends to 2030. (6) Liquidity 'limited': cash EUR28m at end-2025, of which EUR16m restricted, so EUR12m freely available. RCF EUR89m of EUR125m drawn (71%). Material underperformance, working capital swings or extra capex 'may result in a downgrade to the CCC category'. (7) Downgrade sensitivities: no refinancing or credible plan within six months; margins below 20%; negative FCF or tighter liquidity; EBITDA leverage not reduced below 7.5x; interest coverage below 1.5x. (8) Recovery: going-concern EBITDA c.EUR95m at a 5.5x multiple, 10% administrative claims deducted, RCF assumed fully drawn; RR4 for the senior secured TLB and RCF. (9) Business: niche position in premium biometric lenses (B.I.G. Vision, 610 patents, 40% of core sales from highly differentiated products), but small next to EssilorLuxottica, Hoya and Zeiss. Germany is 31% of 2025 sales, and weak demand there leads consumers to delay or trade down premium multifocal purchases. Governance assessed as having 'some deficiencies' (no rating impact).

analysis_pieces.title: Rodenstock explores private credit options for EUR810m TLB refi (9fin, 21-Mar-2025)
analysis_pieces.key_findings: Apax in early-stage talks with banks and private credit funds to refinance EUR810m of TLB debt (EUR660m due May-2028, EUR150m due Jul-2028). Options discussed: a hybrid of syndicated TLB and a junior private credit tranche, or a full large-cap private credit take-out. Both loans priced at E+500bps (2021 and 2022) and were quoted at 95.5. Sources put EBITDA at around EUR135m. Moody's cited FY2023 sales of EUR506m and EBITDA before one-offs of EUR122m. Moody's Apr-2024 outlook change cited credit metrics weaker than expected for at least two years, limited revenue growth despite an expected 2023 turnaround, and the phase-out of the GrandVision contract. Apax and Rodenstock declined to comment. Eighteen months later no refinancing has completed.

analysis_pieces.title: Is Rodenstock seeing clearly? (9fin, 20-May-2021)
analysis_pieces.key_findings: Origination piece for the Apax/Mubadala buyout financing (EUR660m 7-year cov-lite TLB, guided E+475bps, 0% floor, 98.5-99.0 OID; EUR120m RCF). Purchase price EUR1.275bn to Compass, marketed off EUR125m expected 2021 EBITDA (10.2x). Apax c.73%, Mubadala c.24%, founders/management c.3%; EUR610m equity cheque. The RCF carries a 9.5x springing net leverage covenant, tested from 12 months post-closing only if drawn at least 40%. Security: share pledges, bank accounts and intercompany receivables of material subsidiaries; guarantor coverage minimum 80% of group EBITDA. Scale is the recurring structural risk: c.1.9% global market share (2015) against EssilorLuxottica, Hoya and Zeiss. History: 2003 financial difficulties; 2010-11 standstill with RBS and Societe Generale on EUR370m of debt under Bridgepoint, with c.EUR190m of unfunded German pensions; EUR75m shareholder equity injection in Jun-2020. FY2025 EBITDA (c.EUR108m implied by Fitch) is now below the EUR125m the buyout was marketed on.

situation_overview:
Rodenstock's EUR840m TLB (due Jun-2028) and EUR125m RCF (due Dec-2027) have not been refinanced as of 27-Sep-2026. Ciaran has confirmed this directly, and it matches Fitch's 06-Jul-2026 report: Fitch rates the TLB as existing debt, conditions the B- on a refinancing or credible plan within six months (by early Jan-2027), and assumes refinancing only in 2027. Apax has been trying to refinance since Mar-2025. In that time leverage has risen to 8.5x, FCF has been negative, the RCF has been drawn to 71%, and the CEO has left without a named successor.

Business and drivers. Rodenstock is a Munich-based ophthalmic lens maker, owned by Apax (with Mubadala) since the Apr-2021 buyout from Compass Partners and lens-only since the eyewear division was sold to De Rigo in Dec-2022. Fitch credits it with a defensible niche in premium biometric lenses: B.I.G. Vision, 610 patents, 40% of core sales from highly differentiated products, a 61% gross margin and a 22% Fitch-adjusted EBITDA margin. It remains a mid-sized player next to EssilorLuxottica, Hoya and Zeiss. Two headwinds dominate. First, Germany (31% of 2025 sales) is weak, and consumers paying out of pocket for premium multifocals are delaying purchases or trading down. Second, the GrandVision supply contract is being phased out, which Fitch expects to reduce sales again in 2026.

Recent performance. The modest improvement reported for FY2024 has not continued. In FY2024 revenue rose 1.2% on a comparable basis to EUR512.4m and company-adjusted EBITDA rose 5.1% to EUR128.6m. FY2025 sales then fell c.3.8% to EUR493m (Fitch). Fitch describes 2025 as a particularly weak year for FCF, driven by lower EBITDA, higher capex, sizeable interest and material restructuring costs. Fitch's 22% margin implies FY2025 EBITDA of c.EUR108m (analyst calculation). This is not directly comparable with the company-adjusted FY2024 figure, but Fitch states explicitly that EBITDA fell. It is also below the EUR125m the 2021 buyout was marketed on. Fitch puts EBITDA leverage at 8.5x at end-2025. That is well above the indicative 6.3x in revision 1 of this file, which covered TLB debt only, excluded RCF drawings and used the higher company-adjusted FY2024 EBITDA. Rodenstock has not published FY2025 results on 9fin or its press page.

Actions taken. No deleveraging or balance sheet restructuring is on record under Apax. The sponsor has made no equity injection since the 2021 buyout, and none is reported for the refinancing. Operational measures are under way: Fitch cites cost-cutting already executed, footprint optimisation and restructuring costs of EUR10m in 2026. Despite constrained liquidity, the company made a small bolt-on acquisition in Croatia in Mar-2026 (terms undisclosed). Moody's withdrew its Caa1 rating at the issuer's request on 30-Jul-2026, three weeks after Fitch's assignment. No refinancing took place, so the withdrawal was not tied to a completed transaction; no reason was disclosed. Current ratings are Fitch B- (stable) and S&P B- (per the 9fin screener).

Management. There has been significant turnover in the finance function during the refinancing process. CFO Dr. Mani Herold (appointed Apr-2023, formerly CFO of Pfleiderer with a debt capital markets background) left for VTG in Apr-2025. The CEO then covered the CFO role until Dr. Martina Bentele joined from Siemens Energy on 01-Feb-2026. CEO Marcus Desimoni stepped down for personal reasons on 30-Jun-2026. The Executive Management Team and the Advisory Board are running the business while a successor is sought. The refinancing is therefore being led by a CFO eight months into the role, with no permanent CEO.

Near-term outlook. Fitch's base case has sales falling at a low-single-digit rate in 2026, the margin rising to 24.4% on cost savings already executed, leverage of 8.0x in 2026 and 7.7x in 2027, and FCF slightly negative near term. Its own forecasts therefore remain above its 7.5x downgrade sensitivity through 2027. Fitch also assumes the refinancing margin rises by c.100bps (6% vs 5%), which would add to an interest burden already weighing on FCF. The TLBs were quoted at 93.2 on 25-Sep-2026, per the 9fin pricing file in /resources/Rodenstock/. They fell from c.96 to c.88 after the Apr-2025 Moody's downgrade and touched 87.7 in Apr-2026. The market is pricing refinancing risk but not a distressed outcome. There are no earnings call transcripts on 9fin, so management's own outlook is limited to the May-2025 FY2024 release.

key_catalysts.liquidity: Constrained. At end-2025 (Fitch): cash EUR28m, of which EUR16m is restricted, leaving EUR12m freely available. The RCF was EUR89m drawn out of EUR125m, leaving EUR36m undrawn. Accessible liquidity was therefore c.EUR48m (analyst calculation), less than 10% of FY2025 sales of EUR493m. Burn: FCF was negative in 2025 ('particularly weak'), and Fitch expects it to stay slightly negative in the near term. Known cash calls in 2026: restructuring costs of c.EUR10m, pension contributions of EUR11-12m a year, and E+500bps cash interest on c.EUR930m of drawn senior debt. Fitch warns that underperformance, working capital swings or extra capex 'may result in a downgrade to the CCC category'. The 2026 year-to-date liquidity position is not available - further diligence required (source: H1-2026 lender reporting or FY2025 audited accounts). Cross-reference: researcher-capital's liquidity build (capital.json) predates the Fitch report and shows cash and RCF drawings as not available; it should be updated with these figures.

recommendation.rationale: Add to the restructuring watchlist. The maturity wall and liquidity triggers are both present, and the RCF covenant test is live. First, the maturity wall: c.EUR965m of senior secured commitments (EUR840m TLB due Jun-2028, EUR125m RCF due Dec-2027) has not been refinanced after 18 months of sponsor-led effort. The RCF becomes a current liability in Dec-2026 and Fitch's six-month window ends in early Jan-2027. Refinancing the current quantum means lenders taking on 8.5x leverage in a business whose sales fell c.4% in 2025, whose FCF is negative and whose margin will likely step up by c.100bps on any new deal. Fitch's own forecasts keep leverage above its 7.5x downgrade trigger through 2027. That points to a solution involving sponsor equity, a smaller debt quantum or an amend-and-extend, and so to a lender negotiation. Second, liquidity: only c.EUR48m was accessible at end-2025 (EUR12m unrestricted cash plus EUR36m undrawn RCF), with 2026 restructuring costs, pension contributions and interest still to be funded. Fitch explicitly flags a move to the CCC category. Third, the RCF springing covenant is being tested because the facility is 71% drawn; no breach is reported, but headroom cannot be confirmed. Execution risk is higher because the CEO left on 30-Jun-2026 without a named successor and the CFO has been in post since Feb-2026. Moody's had the company at Caa1 before withdrawing. For reference, Fitch's recovery assumptions (EUR95m going-concern EBITDA at 5.5x, less 10% administrative claims) imply a distressed value of c.EUR470m against c.EUR965m of senior secured claims (analyst calculation). The loans trade at 93.2, so the market is not yet pricing that outcome. Next steps: watch for a refinancing launch, an amend-and-extend or a sponsor equity commitment before early Jan-2027; Fitch's review at the end of its six-month window; FY2025 audited accounts and any 2026 interim figures; and the CEO appointment.
triggers: Leverage / maturity wall that cannot be refinanced: PRESENT. EUR840m TLB (Jun-2028, c.21 months) and EUR125m RCF (Dec-2027, c.15 months) NOT refinanced as of 27-Sep-2026. Leverage 8.5x at end-2025 (Fitch); FCF negative; refinancing explored since Mar-2025 without result; Fitch's six-month refinancing condition expires early Jan-2027, and failure could lead to a downgrade (Fitch notes CCC category risk).

Liquidity issue: PRESENT (constrained). End-2025: EUR12m unrestricted cash plus EUR36m undrawn RCF = c.EUR48m. FCF 'particularly weak' in 2025 and expected slightly negative near term; RCF 71% drawn; Fitch assesses liquidity as limited. The 2026 position is not available.

Covenant trip: TEST LIVE, NOT REPORTED AS BREACHED. The TLB is covenant-lite. The RCF's 9.5x springing net leverage covenant (2021 terms) is tested because utilisation is 71%, above the 40% threshold. Covenant-basis leverage and headroom are not available; Fitch's 8.5x gross leverage is within c.1.0x of the trigger on an unadjusted basis.
